question.text: The three primary objectives of SEBI, as stated in the SEBI Act, 1992, include all of the following EXCEPT:

answer.text: Protection of the interests of investors in securities
Promotion of the development of the securities market
Guaranteeing minimum returns to investors in securities

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI Act, 1992, the three statutory objectives of SEBI are (i) to protect the interests of investors in securities, (ii) to promote the development of the securities market, and (iii) to regulate the securities market. SEBI is a market regulator — it does not, and as a matter of regulatory design cannot, guarantee any minimum return to investors. Guaranteeing returns is inconsistent with risk-based, market-priced securities investing and is therefore not among SEBI's statutory objectives. The Trap: The other three options paraphrase SEBI's actual statutory functions (investor protection, market development, market regulation) and are therefore not the "EXCEPT" answer. "Guaranteeing minimum returns" is the odd one out: it conflates investor protection with return assurance, which SEBI has never undertaken to provide. Note: The cited pages of the NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook (p.44, p.73, p.301) reference the no-guaranteed-returns nature of mutual funds and AMFI code rules, but do not enumerate the three statutory objectives of SEBI under the SEBI Act, 1992. The framing above is drawn directly from the SEBI Act, 1992 (Preamble / Section 11) as general regulatory knowledge.
